definition.en: A Special Economic Zone (SEZ) is a geographically delineated area subject to different economic regulations than the rest of the country, designed to boost exports, attract foreign investment, and create employment.
definition.hi: A Special Economic Zone (SEZ) is a geographically delineated area subject to different economic regulations than the rest of the country, designed to boost exports, attract foreign investment, and create employment.

importanceInUpsc.en: SEZs are a critical component of India's industrial infrastructure strategy, frequently appearing in GS-3 Economy questions regarding export competitiveness and manufacturing growth. Understanding the SEZ Act, 2005, and its impact on the Indian economy is essential for analyzing government policies aimed at 'Make in India' and global supply chain integration.

learningOutcomes.en: Analyze the role of SEZs in promoting foreign direct investment and export-led growth.
